about: The epistola of the formulary “14th Sunday after Pentecost” in the 1962 Roman Missal.

seg.tr: Brethren: Walk in the Spirit, and you will not carry out the desires of the flesh. For the flesh sets its desires against the Spirit, and the Spirit against the flesh; for these things are set against one another, so that you do not do all that you wish. But if you are led by the Spirit, you are not under the law. Now the works of the flesh are manifest, which are fornication, impurity, immodesty, debauchery, the service of idols, sorceries, enmities, disputes, rivalries, fits of anger, brawls, dissensions, sects, envies, murders, drunkenness, revelries, and things like these; about which I forewarn you, as I have forewarned you, that those who do such things will not gain the kingdom of God. But the fruit of the Spirit is love, joy, peace, patience, kindness, goodness, long-suffering, mildness, faith, modesty, continence, chastity. Against such things there is no law. And those who are Christ’s have crucified their flesh with its vices and lusts.
